a: GingersAttic is a virtual antique mall. Each seller decorates a booth and lists their own items, and GingersAttic sells them through the GingersAttic store on consignment.

A booth is one seller's own space in the mall: a little room they decorate with wallpaper, flooring, shelves, tables and decor, with their items set out in it. Click an item in a booth to see its photos, price and details.
Small things can sit together in a collectibles box: click the box to see its items up close.
items.source: the booth app; settled fact (one booth per member account)

a: Each item belongs to the seller whose booth it's in. GingersAttic sells it for them through its online store, so you pay GingersAttic, and buyers and sellers deal with each other only through GingersAttic.
GingersAttic collects sales tax on store sales where the law requires it.

items.q: Can I ask a question about an item?
a: Yes: open the item and choose "Ask about this item". Your question goes to GingersAttic, which asks the seller and emails you their answer. Buyers and sellers don't contact each other directly.

items.q: Are the items checked before they go on sale?
a: Yes. GingersAttic approves every item before it goes on sale.

Sellers must use real photos of the actual item, give its measurements and condition, and mention chips, cracks, repairs, missing parts and replaced pieces. If an item is a reproduction or a reissue, or its age isn't known, the seller has to say so.

Everything ships by USPS. USPS calculates shipping at checkout from the item's weight and size, with USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express rates, and sellers ship within 3 business days.

items.q: Do you ship outside the US?
a: Not yet: GingersAttic ships within the US only for now.
All sales are final, so items can't be returned because you changed your mind.
If an item doesn't arrive, or is significantly not as described, GingersAttic may refund you. Contact us below.

items.q: How do I open a booth?
a: Anyone with a member account can open one booth. You decorate it, list your own items, and GingersAttic sells them for you through the GingersAttic store on consignment.
You keep ownership of your items until they sell, and you must own every item you list (or have the owner's permission to sell it).
Yes. GingersAttic reviews every new item before shoppers can see it, and may decline or remove any listing at any time.
Price and quantity changes go live immediately. Changes to photos, the title, the description or the details go back for review; the approved version stays up meanwhile.

A display box for small things such as thimbles, buttons and rings. Choose a wooden crate, a jewelry box or a curio drawer, pick a lining colour and a grid from 2 × 2 to 4 × 4 compartments, and put one item in each compartment.
You can place up to 3 boxes in your booth, and each box counts as one piece of the 40 you can have out at once. Shoppers click a box to see its items up close.

items.q: What does it cost to sell, and when am I paid?
a: GingersAttic keeps a 15% commission on each item's sale price. The shipping the buyer pays at checkout (calculated by USPS from the item's weight and size) is passed to you to cover postage.

Payouts are made once a month for items that have been delivered. An item counts as delivered once you've marked it shipped and either 14 days have passed or GingersAttic has confirmed delivery. GingersAttic will ask you how you'd like to be paid before your first payout.

items.q: What happens when my item sells?
a: You'll get an email and see the order on your My Sales page. Ship it by USPS within 3 business days, packed well enough to survive the trip, and add the tracking number on My Sales. Insured shipping is strongly recommended for anything fragile or over $100.
Shoppers' questions reach you through GingersAttic too: don't share your phone number, email or address, and don't sell outside GingersAttic.
These can't be sold at GingersAttic, even as antiques:
list: Firearms, ammunition, gun parts, explosives, fireworks, and weapons such as switchblades or brass knuckles
Ivory, tortoiseshell, rhino horn, and parts of endangered or protected animals (including feathers and taxidermy of protected species)
Human remains, including skulls, bones and teeth (antique or vintage items made with human hair are allowed when the listing says so)
Hazardous materials: asbestos items, mercury, radioactive items (other than ordinary uranium glass), pesticides and chemicals
Recalled or unsafe children's items: cribs, car seats, baby walkers, toys with lead paint sold for children's use
Alcohol, tobacco, vaping products, drugs, drug paraphernalia, prescription medicine and medical devices
Counterfeits, fakes, and reproductions sold as originals
Stolen goods, and archaeological or cultural artifacts without lawful provenance
Hate-group items, including Nazi and KKK memorabilia
Currency, coins or stamps that are forgeries, and live tickets or gift cards
Items that copy someone else's trademark or artwork without permission
after: Items made with human hair, such as Victorian hair lockets and mourning jewelry, are allowed if they are antique or vintage and the listing says they contain human hair.
GingersAttic may remove prohibited items without notice, and repeated attempts can close your booth.
